  <｜｜DSML｜｜parameter name="oldText" string="true">// ParseDSMLToolCalls extracts all DSML tool calls from text. It returns an
  // error when an <invoke> block is left unclosed (e.g. the response was cut
  // off mid-emission): a truncated call must never be executed.
  //
  // Block pairing comes from dsmlBlockRanges, whose stack scan treats
  // <parameter> bodies as opaque: a literal "<invoke" or "</invoke>" inside a
  // parameter VALUE is content, not structure. This is what the old non-greedy
  // block regex could not deliver - it stopped at the first </invoke> in text
  // order, so a value embedding a DSML example (e.g. a shell snippet carrying
  // "<invoke name=\"x\">...</invoke>") cut the block early and dropped every
  // parameter after it ("missing parameter cmd" in practice).
  func ParseDSMLToolCalls(text string) ([]DSMLCall, error) {
  	text = normalizeDSMLText(text)
  	// Truncation check by state-machine scan: named <invoke> opens are
  	// matched against </invoke> closes in text order, with <parameter>
  	// bodies treated as opaque content (a raw "<invoke" or "</invoke>"
  	// inside a parameter VALUE is content, not structure). A cut-off
  	// emission (an opening tag never closed) must never be executed.
  	// Unlike an opens-vs-closes count, a stray "</invoke>" in prose can
  	// never satisfy an unclosed call (false negative); unlike stripping
  	// complete blocks first, a nested or mis-nested open (two opens, one
  	// close) is still detected instead of being silently swallowed.
  	blocks, unclosed, _, _ := dsmlBlockRanges(text)
  	if unclosed > 0 {
  		return nil, fmt.Errorf("DSML tool call truncated: %d unclosed <invoke>", unclosed)
  	}
  	if len(blocks) == 0 {
  		return nil, nil
  	}

  	var calls []DSMLCall
  	covered := -1 // closeEnd of the most recently parsed top-level block
  	for _, b := range blocks {
  		// A block directly nested inside another one (outside any
  		// <parameter> body - those are opaque to the scan) is a structural
  		// accident, not a second call: executing both would double-run the
  		// inner tool. Skip it here just like StripDSMLToolCalls does.
  		if b.openStart < covered {
  			continue
  		}
  		covered = b.closeEnd
  		body := text[b.openEnd:b.closeStart]
  		// Mask nested blocks inside this body so their <parameter> tags are
  		// invisible to the extraction regex: the enclosing call must not
  		// pick up arguments the model meant for the accidental inner call.
  		for _, c := range blocks {
  			if c.openStart > b.openStart && c.closeEnd < b.closeEnd {
  				s, e := c.openStart-b.openEnd, c.closeEnd-b.openEnd
  				body = body[:s] + strings.Repeat(" ", e-s) + body[e:]
  			}
  		}
  		inv := DSMLCall{Name: dsmlBlockName(text[b.openStart:b.openEnd]), Args: map[string]any{}}
  		for _, pm := range dsmlParamRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(body, -1) {
  			key := pm[1]
  			val := decodeDSMLValue(pm[3], pm[2] == "true")
  			// Repeated parameters mean an array (DeepSeek models emit
  			// <parameter name="justification"> twice for a []string arg).
  			if prev, ok := inv.Args[key]; ok {
  				if arr, isArr := prev.([]any); isArr {
  					inv.Args[key] = append(arr, val)
  				} else {
  					inv.Args[key] = []any{prev, val}
  				}
  			} else {
  				inv.Args[key] = val
  			}
  		}
  		calls = append(calls, inv)
  	}
  	return calls, nil
  }</｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
  <｜｜DSML｜｜parameter name="newText" string="true">// ParseDSMLToolCalls extracts all DSML tool calls from text. It returns an
  // error when an <invoke> block is left unclosed (e.g. the response was cut
  // off mid-emission): a truncated call must never be executed.
  //
  // Block pairing comes from dsmlBlockRanges, whose stack scan treats
  // <parameter> bodies as opaque: a literal "<invoke" or "</invoke>" inside a
  // parameter VALUE is content, not structure. This is what the old non-greedy
  // block regex could not deliver - it stopped at the first </invoke> in text
  // order, so a value embedding a DSML example (e.g. a shell snippet carrying
  // "<invoke name=\"x\">...</invoke>") cut the block early and dropped every
  // parameter after it ("missing parameter cmd" in practice).
  //
  // ParseDSMLMessage uses parseDSMLToolCallsStrict instead - it additionally
  // learns which strict-format violations a successful parse still contains.
  func ParseDSMLToolCalls(text string) ([]DSMLCall, error) {
  	calls, err, _ := parseDSMLToolCallsStrict(text)
  	return calls, err
  }

  // dsmlViolations records whether a parse hit each of the strict-format
  // violations (bool summary; the caller only needs "any violation happened").
  type dsmlViolations struct {
  	justification      bool // parameter carries the decorative justification key
  	normalizeChanged   bool // normalizeDSMLText repaired markup (normalized != original)
  	strayClose         bool // extra </invoke> close tag left outside any block
  	implicitClose      bool // a missing </invoke> was closed implicitly at the wrapper close
  	wrapperTypo        bool // wrapper close was cut off or spelled with a typo'd tag
  	bareInvoke         bool // complete invoke blocks with no tool_calls wrapper at all
  	missingStringAttr  bool // a <parameter> omitted its string attribute
  	nestedMask         bool // a parameter value embedded a nested invoke block (masked)
  }

  // any reports whether at least one strict-format violation happened.
  func (v dsmlViolations) any() bool {
  	return v.justification || v.normalizeChanged || v.strayClose || v.implicitClose ||
  		v.wrapperTypo || v.bareInvoke || v.missingStringAttr || v.nestedMask
  }

  // dsmlToolCallsStrictCloseRe matches the EXACT, correctly-spelled wrapper
  // close tag at the very end of the text. The looser dsmlToolCallsCloseEndRe
  // also admits typo'd/whitespace variants (</_calls>, <calls>, </ tool_calls >)
  // that are still an "emission complete" signal for execution, but count as a
  // strict-format violation here.
  var dsmlToolCallsStrictCloseRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)</tool_calls>\s*$`)

  // parseDSMLToolCallsStrict is ParseDSMLToolCalls plus strict-format violation
  // tracking. The parse itself is unchanged from the public entry point - a
  // call that parses still parses, and the same truncated/unparseable shapes
  // still error - so the violation flags only describe HOW strictly the model
  // followed the required format, never whether the call is executable.
  func parseDSMLToolCallsStrict(text string) ([]DSMLCall, error, dsmlViolations) {
  	var viol dsmlViolations
  	original := text
  	text = normalizeDSMLText(text)
  	if text != original {
  		viol.normalizeChanged = true
  	}
  	// Truncation check by state-machine scan: named <invoke> opens are
  	// matched against </invoke> closes in text order, with <parameter>
  	// bodies treated as opaque content (a raw "<invoke" or "</invoke>"
  	// inside a parameter VALUE is content, not structure). A cut-off
  	// emission (an opening tag never closed) must never be executed.
  	// Unlike an opens-vs-closes count, a stray "</invoke>" in prose can
  	// never satisfy an unclosed call (false negative); unlike stripping
  	// complete blocks first, a nested or mis-nested open (two opens, one
  	// close) is still detected instead of being silently swallowed.
  	blocks, unclosed, _, strays, implicitClose := dsmlBlockRangesStrict(text)
  	if len(strays) > 0 {
  		viol.strayClose = true
  	}
  	if implicitClose {
  		viol.implicitClose = true
  	}
  	if unclosed > 0 {
  		return nil, fmt.Errorf("DSML tool call truncated: %d unclosed <invoke>", unclosed), viol
  	}
  	if len(blocks) == 0 {
  		return nil, nil, viol
  	}

  	var calls []DSMLCall
  	covered := -1 // closeEnd of the most recently parsed top-level block
  	for _, b := range blocks {
  		// A block directly nested inside another one (outside any
  		// <parameter> body - those are opaque to the scan) is a structural
  		// accident, not a second call: executing both would double-run the
  		// inner tool. Skip it here just like StripDSMLToolCalls does.
  		if b.openStart < covered {
  			continue
  		}
  		covered = b.closeEnd
  		body := text[b.openEnd:b.closeStart]
  		// Mask nested blocks inside this body so their <parameter> tags are
  		// invisible to the extraction regex: the enclosing call must not
  		// pick up arguments the model meant for the accidental inner call.
  		for _, c := range blocks {
  			if c.openStart > b.openStart && c.closeEnd < b.closeEnd {
  				viol.nestedMask = true
  				s, e := c.openStart-b.openEnd, c.closeEnd-b.openEnd
  				body = body[:s] + strings.Repeat(" ", e-s) + body[e:]
  			}
  		}
  		inv := DSMLCall{Name: dsmlBlockName(text[b.openStart:b.openEnd]), Args: map[string]any{}}
  		for _, pm := range dsmlParamRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(body, -1) {
  			key := pm[1]
  			if pm[2] == "" {
  				viol.missingStringAttr = true
  			}
  			val := decodeDSMLValue(pm[3], pm[2] == "true")
  			// Repeated parameters mean an array (DeepSeek models emit
  			// <parameter name="justification"> twice for a []string arg).
  			if prev, ok := inv.Args[key]; ok {
  				if arr, isArr := prev.([]any); isArr {
  					inv.Args[key] = append(arr, val)
  				} else {
  					inv.Args[key] = []any{prev, val}
  				}
  			} else {
  				inv.Args[key] = val
  			}
  		}
  		if _, ok := inv.Args["justification"]; ok {
  			viol.justification = true
  		}
  		calls = append(calls, inv)
  	}
  	// Wrapper-shape judgement (violations #5 and #6). A cut-off close tag,
  	// a typo'd close tag, or a missing wrapper close entirely are all
  	// "intended as a tool call" (IsDSMLToolCallReply) but not the strict
  	// format. The strict close regex is the only clean shape.
  	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(text)
  	switch {
  	case IsDSMLToolCallCut(original):
  		viol.wrapperTypo = true
  	case !dsmlToolCallsCloseEndRe.MatchString(trimmed):
  		viol.bareInvoke = true
  	case !dsmlToolCallsStrictCloseRe.MatchString(trimmed):
  		viol.wrapperTypo = true
  	}
  	return calls, nil, viol
  }</｜｜DSML｜｜parameter>
  </｜｜DSML｜｜invoke>
